data.reason: The gate REFUSES (exit 3): the whole suite has not passed on this tree because ci is skipped (the merged tree's lint is red in main's tests/test_brief_recovery_slice.py, another lane's file). The change-reached suites run green locally: tests/test_roborev_wait.py (22 passed), tests/test_roborev_branch.py, tests/test_standards_roborev_agent.py (66 passed together on the branch head), the pinned selection for both leased files, and all 16 wait tests fail against the unfixed module.

chunk_findings.detail: The updated live note still tells the user to run `python -m ddflow.services.roborev wait --job {job}` without preserving the repository scope. If the roborev job was enqueued against `/path/to/repo` (for example via `--repo /path/to/repo`) but the suggested follow-up command is run from another directory or worktree, the CLI will resolve the current directory instead of the job’s repository and can report that the job does not exist / exit 2, even though the job exists. The previous triage confirmed this omission and said the fix would name the repo, but this diff still omits `--repo` in the printed advice, so the trap remains.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/roborev.py:_live

chunk_findings.detail: The follow-up command is built by interpolating the repository path without shell quoting. If the repository path contains spaces (for example `[REDACTED:path] repo` or `C:\Users\My Repo`), the printed advice is `python -m ddflow.services.roborev wait --job 7 --repo [REDACTED:path] repo`; when copied into a shell, argparse sees an extra positional token `repo` (or, if `wait` is omitted, consumes it as the optional `wait` token and then rejects it as an unknown command) and the command fails, or at best scopes to only `[REDACTED:path]`. Thus the “one sure way forward” advice is not runnable for such repositories; the path needs to be quoted.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/roborev.py:_live

chunk_findings.detail: The fallback job-id lookup now uses the `jobs` list captured before `roborev review` runs. If the enqueue output does not contain a parseable `job <id>`, `_find_job` can only return a job that was already present in that pre-enqueue list. Because `_reusable_job` returned `None` before enqueueing, any matching record is by definition not reusable (e.g. an earlier `failed` job for the same head). Example: the pre-read list contains job 100 with `git_ref=head` and status `failed`; `_reusable_job` returns None; `roborev review --since mb` succeeds but prints only "queued" (no job id); the regex fails and the fallback returns 100. `_collect` then waits/collects job 100 and records its failure, while the actual newly enqueued job (101) is ignored. If no such stale record exists, `_find_job` returns None even though the enqueue succeeded, whereas the previous code re-listed after enqueue and could find the new job. This can record a wrong result or unavailable instead of the standards-gate job id.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/roborev_branch.py:_find_job

chunk_findings.detail: `wait_job` calls `_settled(rec, job)` on the very first list read with no memory of whether the job was ever seen. If `roborev list --json` has not yet indexed a just-enqueued job—e.g. `roborev review <sha>` prints `job 2917` but the next list query does not include it yet—then `rec` is `None` and `_settled` returns the terminal `no job ... re-run review` result. `main` exits 2 immediately, before consuming any of `wait_s`. This can record the job unavailable and cause a duplicate enqueue for a job that appears moments later.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/roborev.py:wait_job

chunk_findings.detail: For an unknown non-empty status (any roborev state not in `_UNFINISHED`, `_ENDED`, or `"done"`), `_settled` returns a `WaitResult` instead of `None`, so `wait_job(where, job, 300)` aborts after one poll with `live=False` and exit 2. The function’s own doc says it returns `None` when the job is still queued/running (“wait goes on”), and the branch comment says the unknown status “may still be live”; returning a terminal `WaitResult` stops the wait before the bound instead of continuing to poll.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/roborev.py:_settled

chunk_findings.detail: The new `rec is None` and `status in _ENDED` notes build the follow-up command `roborev review <sha of the branch head>` without `--repo`/the resolved `where`. If the wait was `python -m ddflow.services.roborev wait --job 7 --repo /path/to/repo` run from `/other`, those notes advise a command that, executed from `/other`, enqueues against `/other` rather than `/path/to/repo`. The `_live` note already preserves the repository; these new notes do not.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/roborev.py:_settled

chunk_findings.detail: The fallback that “one fresh read finds it” is gated on `if job is None`, not on “enqueue output had no parseable id.” In the confirmed scenario this does not answer the probe: the pre-enqueue `jobs` list contains an earlier failed job 100 for the same head, `_reusable_job` returns `None`, `roborev review` exits 0 with no `job <id>` in its output, and `_find_job(jobs, where, head, q.stdout + q.stderr)` still returns the stale failed job 100. Since `job` is not `None`, the new fresh `_list` read is skipped, so `_collect` still waits on stale failed job 100 instead of the just-enqueued job. The fix must use “output had no parseable id” as the trigger for the fresh read, or `_find_job` must return `None` when its only match came from the pre-enqueue list.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/roborev_branch.py:179

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to prove that negative `--wait-s` does not silently become the 900s config default, but it writes `DONE` into the status file before running `RR.main`. A done job produces exactly one `list --json` read and exit 0 whether the effective wait is -5, 0, or 900, so the assertions cannot distinguish the allowed one-poll behavior from the forbidden default substitution. Under the very bug the test is meant to catch, this test would still pass.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_roborev_wait.py::test_main_keeps_a_negative_wait_s_negative

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `"ended " not in out.note` only rejects the word `ended` when it is followed by a space. If `out.note` ends with the banned word—for example `"job 7 has no readable status; ended"`—the substring `"ended "` is absent while `"no readable status"` is present, so the test passes even though the note does classify the job as ended. The guard does not enforce the invariant stated in the docstring.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_roborev_wait.py::test_a_job_without_a_readable_status_is_unchecked_not_ended
